platformClippy.meaning: Current host observation only, separate from the later immutable execution candidate. File attribution does not prove that diagnostics in a modified historical file were introduced by Phase 19. Whole-platform strict status and the independent business crate status are distinct.

limitations: Scoped PG excludes the independent notification live suite and is not a complete postgres gate.

Node-free proof reuses the original ELF under UID10001 with no published ports or workspace mounts, in a writable transport rootfs. It proves bounded startup/health/401/503 behavior; successful real platform member assignment belongs to the separate actual joint suite.
Actual PASS applies only to this immutable candidate. Development Windows/Node failures and separate strict platform Clippy diagnostics retain their own source and environment boundaries.

Both adopted PostgreSQL and full-fast outer runners actually passed, including their four owner-label empty-resource queries and stopped WSL leases. The superseded candidate cancellation remains an original FAIL with its separate source digest and contributes no adopted counts.

The superseded r2 PostgreSQL PASS, full-fast FAIL (original ci-policy failure) and raw runtime PASS retain their own common source digest, capture drivers, complete reports/logs, original ELF and cleanup records. Their counts are never combined with the final candidate results.
The index binds successful, failed and development evidence. Listing an artifact never changes its original status, environment or source boundary.

The archive excludes immutable source-tree copies, node_modules and build caches. Candidate manifests and archived capture/execution drivers bind those sources without copying them into the artifact index.

This publication certifies only the adopted candidate and the boundary-defined current owned inputs rechecked here; it does not certify all shared host bytes, future phases, registry publication, traffic cutover or production deployment.
